items.title: Apollo private credit fund sees redemption requests fall in Q3
items.takeaway: Redemption requests at Apollo Global Management’s flagship private credit vehicle fell in the third quarter, providing another indication that the liquidity pressures affecting non-traded private credit funds may be starting to moderate, according to a report by Reuters.
items.whyItMatters: Apollo is a private-credit heavyweight whose insurance arm, Athene, supplies long-term capital, which makes it central to the fusion of insurance and private lending. Private credit's rapid growth draws regulatory attention; loan quality and valuations are the key things to watch. For allocators: private credit offers high floating-rate income but less liquidity, so manager selection and underwriting discipline matter.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 2.68%, historically tight (up 2 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Sep 22.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.
